official_onet_description: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.
ai_preliminary_reason: No safe shortlisted equivalent; do not interpret as ESCO absence.

official_onet_description: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.
ai_preliminary_reason: ESCO definition closely tracks attention, understanding, and appropriate questioning; confirm ontology scope.

official_onet_description: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.
ai_preliminary_reason: ESCO writing techniques concerns narrative/story techniques; O*NET Writing means written communication appropriate for audience.

official_onet_description: Talking to others to convey information effectively.
ai_preliminary_reason: Public presentations are narrower than the general ability to convey information orally.

official_onet_description: Using mathematics to solve problems.
ai_preliminary_reason: Prior approved mapping retained, but ESCO mathematics is a knowledge concept while O*NET Mathematics is applying mathematics to solve problems; category mismatch.

official_onet_description: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.
ai_preliminary_reason: Top candidate science disciplines do not equal application of scientific methods broadly.

official_onet_description: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.
ai_preliminary_reason: ESCO defines critical evaluation of credibility/evidence and independent judgement; close conceptual alignment.

official_onet_description: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.
ai_preliminary_reason: Teaching students how to learn differs from adapting ones own learning.

official_onet_description: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.
ai_preliminary_reason: ESCO is about using strategies to learn, while O*NET focuses on selecting training/instruction methods; related but not necessarily same.

official_onet_description: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.
ai_preliminary_reason: Shortlist predominantly describes monitoring specific objects/operations, not general assessment of performance.

official_onet_description: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.
ai_preliminary_reason: Training healthcare users in social perception is not the broad ability to infer others reactions.

official_onet_description: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.
ai_preliminary_reason: No safe generalized equivalent in retrieved shortlist.

official_onet_description: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.
ai_preliminary_reason: Presenting arguments is a persuasive subskill, but O*NET includes changing others minds/behavior in varied situations.

official_onet_description: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.
ai_preliminary_reason: Political negotiation is context-specific and narrower than general negotiation.

official_onet_description: Teaching others how to do something.
ai_preliminary_reason: Teaching or guiding others closely corresponds to O*NET instructing.

official_onet_description: Actively looking for ways to help people.
ai_preliminary_reason: Client orientation supports needs and satisfaction but may focus business context vs general willingness to help.

official_onet_description: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.
ai_preliminary_reason: General solve problems lacks explicit novelty, complexity and systems constraints.

official_onet_description: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.
ai_preliminary_reason: Operational research is a discipline/knowledge area, not O*NET task of analyzing needs and requirements for creating designs.

official_onet_description: Generating or adapting equipment and technology to serve user needs.
ai_preliminary_reason: No general equivalence found among retrieved candidates.

official_onet_description: Determining the kind of tools and equipment needed to do a job.
ai_preliminary_reason: Domain-specific equipment selection not broad enough.

official_onet_description: Installing equipment, machines, wiring, or programs to meet specifications.
ai_preliminary_reason: Domain-specific installation tasks not general equivalent.

official_onet_description: Writing computer programs for various purposes.
ai_preliminary_reason: ICT system programming is narrower and specific to systems; O*NET programming spans different purposes.

official_onet_description: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.
ai_preliminary_reason: Monitoring machine operation is narrower than general monitoring of gauges/dials/indicators.

official_onet_description: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.
ai_preliminary_reason: ESCO is focused on control systems and electrical/electronic equipment, narrower than O*NET general operation/control.

official_onet_description: Performing routine maintenance on equipment and determining when and what kind of maintenance is needed.
ai_preliminary_reason: Routine inspection and maintenance for equipment function corresponds closely to O*NET.

official_onet_description: Determining causes of operating errors and deciding what to do about it.
ai_preliminary_reason: Both identify operating problems and decide remedies, though ESCO mentions reporting.

official_onet_description: Repairing machines or systems using the needed tools.
ai_preliminary_reason: No broad match found; shortlisted repair activities are domain-specific.

official_onet_description: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.
ai_preliminary_reason: Both concepts involve inspection/testing to assess products/processes/services.

official_onet_description: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.
ai_preliminary_reason: Generic choosing alternatives does not explicitly evaluate relative costs and benefits.

official_onet_description: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.
ai_preliminary_reason: ESCO addresses assessing impact of system changes on outcomes; close match to O*NET systems analysis.

official_onet_description: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.
ai_preliminary_reason: Retrieved assessment/grading concepts do not assess system performance measures.

official_onet_description: Managing one's own time and the time of others.
ai_preliminary_reason: ESCO includes scheduling events and other people; O*NET defines managing ones own and others time; likely close but scope may differ.

official_onet_description: Determining how money will be spent to get the work done, and accounting for these expenditures.
ai_preliminary_reason: ESCO is a knowledge discipline; O*NET refers to determining expenditures and accounting for spending.

official_onet_description: Obtaining and seeing to the appropriate use of equipment, facilities, and materials needed to do certain work.
ai_preliminary_reason: ESCO manages broad physical resources, O*NET emphasises appropriate use of equipment/facilities/materials.

official_onet_description: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.
ai_preliminary_reason: Recruitment/motivation/development matches part of O*NET, but ESCO includes much wider HR functions.
